title: Temperature stays put while a substance melts or boils
summary: While a substance is melting or boiling, the energy goes into the change of state, so the temperature does not rise until that change is finished.
body: OpenStax Physics says that adding energy sometimes does not change the temperature at all. The extra energy loosens bonds and causes a phase change. Energy that enters or leaves during that change without a temperature change is called latent heat, and the page says latent means hidden. Melting needs energy to break bonds in the solid, so the kinetic energy of the particles does not rise, and neither does the temperature, until the change is finished. The same is true for vaporizing a liquid. In a cup with ice, the page says the temperature stays at the melting temperature until the ice is gone. The size of that hidden energy for water is a NIST row on the linked cards and is not copied here.
